body:
Wow, that's pretty neat.

How does the `<../um/windows.h>` relative path thingy work?
Might warrant a short comment.

WDYT about this approach @bruvzg? I think it's better than #116690 as we don't need to worry about future `windows.h` includes or thirdparty libs.

The approach suggested by @lawnjelly could also be worth looking into, we probably don't need a lot of `windows.h` in our own headers at least, where I assume we mostly need typedefs for `DWORD`, etc., which we could forward-declare or include via `windefs.h`. But this can be a follow-up, IMO this PR seems to be a good first step.

It is cleaner than #116690, and should work with all third-party code which might cause the same issues in the future, so as long as relative path for MSVC is working reliably (have not tested it) it's probably better.

> The approach suggested by @lawnjelly could also be worth looking into

For some places it might be worth doing. But I'm not sure if all smaller headers are the same in MinGW and Windows SDK, and won't change (Windows docs do list some of them, but always have `(include Windows.h)` note).
